# Introduction

We strongly recommend the authors to use the templates provided, either the .docx or the .tex. No paper will be accepted in another template.

Here you should write your introduction, including the literature review. In these guidelines we present an example for the structure of a research paper. However, the names of these sections can be changed by the authors. The Brazilian Journal of Biometrics publishes papers strongly connected with statistical, mathematical and data science methodology, with application to biological sciences.

# Materials and Methods

Here you should describe your data and the methodologies used in the analysis. The details should be enough for the results to be reproducible by the reader. You can include subsections and subsubsections.

## Example of a Subsection

This is an example of a Subsection.

### Example of a Subsubsection

This is an example of a Subsubsection.

# Results and Discussion

Here you should describe your results and their discussion. The discussion can be included as a separate section.

## Equations

Equation numbering, whenever necessary, must be sequential and in Arabic numbers aligned on the right. Its components must be in italics, except for numbers and functions.

$$
DIC = \hat{D} + 2p_{D}
$$ {#eq-dic}

## Figures and tables

@fig-bjb shows the logo of the Brazilian Journal of Biometrics. All figures and tables should have detailed captions and labels to be cited in the text.

![The caption of the figures should be given below the figures. The caption should be detailed enough for the figure to be understood.](figures/bjb_logo.png){#fig-bjb width=50%}

## References

All references must be cited in the text using `[@key]` for inline references such as [@pereira2021naive], and using `@key` for text references such as @zhang2022zero or @pereira2021naive. When citing two or more references in the text you can use [@deng2021estimation; @huang2021causal].

All references should be listed in alphabetical order of the first authors' surname. Examples of citations for books are: @bolle2013guide and @jain2007handbook.

# Conclusions

Here you should present the conclusions of your work and explain how the results will contribute to the field.
